title: Use of English II
description: The General Studies course in effective communication and literary appreciation: the English sound system, stress and syllables, intonation and rhythm, literature and figures of speech, prose fiction, drama and poetry appreciation, and punctuation and forms of writing. Built from Effective Communication and Literary Appreciation Skills (the GES 201 textbook, Centre for General Studies, 2019), the 2025/26 course outline and reading list, and the punctuation slides.

topics.title: The English Sound System
topics.summary: Speaking is a productive skill. English speech sounds are made by the human articulators and divide into 20 vowels (12 pure vowels and 8 diphthongs, plus triphthongs) and 24 consonants, described by the state of the glottis, the place of articulation and the manner of articulation.
subtopics: Vowels and how they are described

topics.title: Syllables and Stress
topics.summary: The suprasegmental features of English work above the individual sound. The syllable is the smallest pronounceable unit, made of an onset, a nucleus and a coda. Stress is the prominence given to a syllable; English stress is free, with patterns for two- and three-syllable words, suffixes, word-class pairs and compounds.
subtopics: Stress in two- and three-syllable words
Suffixes that take, shift or keep stress

topics.title: Intonation and Rhythm
topics.summary: Intonation is the variation of pitch in speech, with four main tunes: rise, fall, rise-fall and fall-rise. The tone-unit has a pre-head, head, tonic syllable and tail. Intonation has grammatical, attitudinal, accentual and discourse functions. English is stress-timed, with feet and weak forms, while most Nigerian languages are syllable-timed.

topics.title: Literature, Its Elements and Figures of Speech
topics.summary: Literature is creative or imaginative work, written or spoken, that depicts human conditions through language marked by indirectness. It entertains, teaches morals, preserves history, builds language proficiency and is therapeutic. Its three genres are drama, poetry and prose, its elements include subject matter, theme, plot, setting and character, and writers use figures of speech.

topics.title: Prose Fiction
topics.summary: Prose, from the Latin prosa (straightforward), tells stories in narrative form. Fiction is an imaginative narrative, while non-fiction gives a true life account. Fiction takes the forms of flash fiction, short story, novella and novel, and its elements are subject matter, theme, plot, characterisation, point of view and setting.
subtopics: Definition and origins of prose fiction
Types of character and of novel

topics.title: Drama and Poetry Appreciation
topics.summary: Drama is literature realised through performance: dialogue, action, characters and stage. Its main types are tragedy, comedy and tragicomedy. Poetry is written in lines and stanzas and marked by rhythm, imagery and sound. Appreciating a poem means examining its subject matter, theme, mood, imagery and figures of speech. The set texts are Synge's Riders to the Sea and eight selected poems.
subtopics: Appreciating a play: Riders to the Sea

topics.title: Punctuation and Forms of Writing
topics.summary: Punctuation marks divide written language into readable bits: full stop, question and exclamation marks, capital letters, comma, apostrophe, colon, semicolon, quotation marks, brackets, hyphen, dash and slash. Forms of writing include official correspondence (formal letters, memos, minutes and reports) and essays, term papers and book reviews.
subtopics: Full stop, question and exclamation marks
Quotation marks, brackets, hyphen, dash and slash
Official correspondence: letters, memos, minutes and reports
Essays, term papers and book reviews
